segments.title: Chương 187: Tam Quốc Sát Lọt Top 10 Bảng Xếp Hạng Tháng
segments.content:
Chapter 190-0187 Sanguosha Breaks into the Top of the Monthly Rankings

In his past life, for that leader Qu Guohao, what Chen Guiliang had him do was the "Sanguosha Collegiate League."

Originally, it didn't have the word "National." The first season was only held in Beijing and Shanghai!

But Qu Guohao reported that Sanguosha enthusiasts in other regions were very dissatisfied that teams were only being selected from Beijing and Shanghai.

So, he proposed another plan.

Qu Guohao used the Yangtze River as a boundary, dividing the national league into Northern and Southern regions.

Then, based on the number of universities in the provinces of the north and south, he adjusted the provinces that straddled the Yangtze. For example, Anhui was designated as the Northern Division, and Jiangsu as the Southern Division.

"Sanguosha OL" also had to cooperate by creating 1v1 and 3v3 match modes.

Next, it was divided into three stages: open qualifiers, regional finals, and the grand finals.

Universities with board game clubs or Sanguosha clubs could obtain registration eligibility for the qualifiers by providing proof of their school club status. They would organize their own campus tournaments to determine the players representing their university and form a team to compete.

The campus qualifier format was face-to-face play with physical cards.

Next was the online group stage: the representative teams from each university were grouped within their respective divisions. Eight teams formed a group for a round-robin tournament, with the top two teams from each group advancing. (During random allocation, if a group had fewer than eight teams, only the first-place team could advance).

All advancing teams would compete in online knockout rounds to determine the southern top eight and northern top eight.

The above constituted the qualifier schedule.

Next came the regional finals, which included an online round-robin and offline knockout rounds, from which the national top four would emerge.

The top four would participate in the national grand finals.

Due to technical and cost limitations, online games at this time did not have a spectator mode.

Take "Warcraft III" for example, a replay file could only be generated five minutes after a match ended to be broadcast or downloaded.

The Sanguosha online qualifiers, which began on October 1st, also generated replay files after matches concluded. Internet users with good speeds could download the replays, while those with poor speeds just followed the text-and-image live update threads.

Campus networks, the Sanguosha Baidu Tieba, the board game Baidu Tieba, and 17173 all had text-and-image live update threads, posted by Game Science staff.

The board game clubs of major universities reposted them to their own BBS forums.

Exciting matches would even be edited into separate clips and posted on video websites like Tudou.

"The first round of the 1v1 match has concluded. Guizhou Finance has defeated Guangdong Tech. The match replay is being generated..."

The open qualifiers at major universities across the country were taking place online at the same time.

Chen Guiliang stood behind the text-and-image commentator, watching the match replay with him.

Qu Guohao said beside Chen Guiliang, "Sanguosha is applying to join the CEG. But it can only be registered as a casual game, like Go, Chinese chess, and Dou Dizhu."

"It doesn't matter if it gets in or not," Chen Guiliang said.

CEG, also known as the China Electronic Sports Games, was hosted by the All-China Sports Federation.

However, last year the State Administration of Radio, Film, and Television had banned TV programs related to online games, halting CCTV-5's "Electronic Sports World." No satellite TV stations could broadcast this stuff.

Without satellite broadcast, the CEG's development was difficult.

Qu Guohao said, "It's still useful if we get in. It would allow 'Sanguosha' to appear publicly in many places."

"What about GameFY?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Qu Guohao said, "We'd have to pay them. I'm negotiating now."

Chen Guiliang said, "Ask the Foreign Language Teaching and Research Press for sponsorship money. It will help them sell the cards."

"I'll give it a try," Qu Guohao said.

Qu Guohao had already been incredibly effective. He had managed to secure a title sponsorship from Motorola without a word to anyone.

Therefore, this competition should be called the "Motorola Cup First National Sanguosha Collegiate League."

However, the sponsorship fee was very low, only a mere 500,000 yuan. Additionally, each player on the champion and runner-up teams would be awarded a Motorola mobile phone.

Just then, an employee shouted, "17173's September rankings are out! Not only did 'Sanguosha' make the top ten, it's ranked ninth!"

"Yeah!"

"Hooray!"

Many employees stopped their work and cheered in celebration.

"Sanguosha" had been on monthly game rankings before, but not 17173's.

Currently, only 17173's monthly ranking was the most authoritative, as it was a comprehensive ranking and was less susceptible to manipulation by game companies.

This ranking was determined by metrics such as on-site search volume, game section traffic, player votes, and editor scores.

The top ten for the September list were: World of Warcraft, Fantasy Westward Journey, The Legend of Mir 2, Audition Online, JX Online, Westward Journey Online II, MapleStory, The World of Legend, Sanguosha, and PopTag.

Although Sanguosha was ranked ninth, it didn't mean its profitability was also ninth.

This was determined by the game's genre and monetization model.

The profits of "Sanguosha," ranked ninth, were certainly far less than "Lineage II," which ranked twelfth.

Chen Guiliang looked closely at the list and surprisingly saw President Shi's "Zhengtu."

That game was only a half-finished product and wouldn't be launched for another six months or more, yet they were already spending money to generate hype. First, they paid to open a special section on 17173 and released a large amount of game information. Then, they hired an online water army to boost activity in the section, had them frantically vote for and search for the game, and promoted its free-to-play model everywhere...

They had forcefully pushed a game that wasn't even finished to the 13th position on the most authoritative game ranking.

Chen Guiliang couldn't help but sigh: Being rich really lets you do whatever you want!

His phone rang. It was Tao Chenggang.

Tao Chenggang's excited voice came from the other end: "'Quan Yu Tianxia' made it onto the 17173 monthly list!"

"Quan Yu Tianxia" was Brother Gang's game. This terrible name was chosen by netizen votes.

First, 20 names were selected from a mess of potential game titles. Then, voting continued: 20 to 10, 10 to 7, 7 to 5... Coinciding with the popular broadcast of "Super Girl," this format was extremely popular, and netizens were very enthusiastic about voting.

Subsequently, Tao Chenggang collaborated with 17173 and opened a game section for "Quan Yu Tianxia." Any netizen who had participated in the final few rounds of voting for the game's name went crazy voting for this game on 17173.

Moreover, people came every day to check in and post, even offering their own suggestions for the game.

Just 23 days after its section opened, it had fought its way to 18th place on the 17173 monthly list.

The two games ahead of it were "Blade & Sword Online" and "Water Margin Q," and the two behind it were "Seal Online" and "EVE."

Chen Guiliang returned to his office and read the 17173 editor's comments.

The editor's comment on "Sanguosha" was: "A unique card game that, while referencing the core rules of 'BANG!', has forged its own path and is a completely different game from 'BANG!'. Its online version is particularly innovative, and its monetization model can serve as a template for similar games. Since first appearing on the list, it has steadily advanced from 18th place, and in September, it has finally broken into the top 10."

The editor's comment on "Zhengtu" was: "A game still in production that broke into the top 15 in its very first appearance on the list. A true dark horse."

The editor's comment on "Quan Yu Tianxia" was: "This game is special. As far as I know, the creator sold 8 internet cafes and 1 car, and is already preparing to sell his house. Fortunately, he secured an investment. The players have watched it grow from nothing, and even the game's name was decided by netizen votes. Many people are looking forward to its release, myself included."

Chen Guiliang switched to the Sanguosha section on 17173. The activity today was particularly high.

"Fellow killers, a historic moment has arrived! Through everyone's efforts, Sanguosha has finally broken into the top ten of the monthly rankings."

"Haha, I'm so excited too. I came every day to search, post, and vote. All to increase Sanguosha's search volume, clicks, and votes."

"We have to keep it up, everyone. It's only 9th place now. Let's aim to break into the top five next month."

"Let's forget about the top five. Those are all monsters."

"I think we can take down 'Legend.' 'Legend' dropped off the list a long time ago. The only reason it's back at number three is because of a game update and an anniversary event. The problem is, the version they updated to isn't the official Korean version at all; it's something Shanda just messed around with. Monsters are copied, maps are stitched together. Everyone in the game is cursing them out right now."
